[0] As vibecoding becomes more widespread, the number of new apps hitting the App Store has surged, doubling in the first half of 2026 — yet downloads grew by just 2%. Here's the full rundown.

[1] New app submissions surge, but downloads lag far behind

[2] A report published today by The New York Times, citing fresh data from Sensor Tower, notes that while new App Store submissions doubled in the first half of 2026, downloads rose by only 2%.

[3] The report also spotlights two developers who have been shipping vibecoded apps on the App Store: Marco Pérez, who plans to leave his job at JPMorgan next month to work on apps full-time, and David Svensson, who has launched 11 niche apps over the past five months and treats vibecoding as a hobby rather than a business.

[4] Excerpt from the report:

[5] Mr. Pérez, a software engineer based in Chicago who had never previously built a mobile app, spent five weeks over the winter exploring "vibecoding" AI tools to create a prototype, then two more weeks preparing it for the App Store. That app, InfoDrizzle, performed decently, racking up 1,300 downloads and earning about $500 in profit. Mr. Pérez's next app was even more popular. In May, he spent roughly a week launching Stampa, a scrapbooking app that turns photos into digital stamps. Stampa has since been downloaded 20,000 times, generating around $3,000 in profit.

[6] Apple spokesperson Peter Ajemian, responding to The New York Times, addressed another issue stemming from the surge in submissions: earlier reports indicated that the App Store review process has come under strain as a result.

[7] "Apple has consistently been able to review 90% of app submissions within 48 hours," Ajemian said, adding that Apple is "delighted to see a new generation of developers using the latest tools to build and ship apps at an unprecedented pace."

[8] He also noted that all apps "must meet the same high standards of quality, privacy, and safety that users have always relied on, regardless of whether they were developed with vibecoding."
